newsitem.title: UK: UK party challenges Major with TV celebrity.
newsitem.headline: UK party challenges Major with TV celebrity.

text.p: Britain's Referendum Party on Saturday named an environmentalist television celebrity to stand against Prime Minister John Major in his parliamentary constituency at the upcoming general election.

The party founded by billionaire tycoon Sir James Goldsmith said David Bellamy, a bearded 63-year-old known for his somewhat eccentric television manner, was its prospective candidate for the Huntingdon constituency.
The Referendum Party, which plans to field 550 candidates at the election expected to be held on May 1, wants a plebiscite on the future role of Britain in the European community.

Major had a huge majority of 36,230 in the Cambridgeshire constituency at the last election in 1992, when he beat off challenges from opponents who included Lord Sutch of the Monster Raving Loony Party and Lord Buckethead of the Gremloid Party.

The attraction of Huntingdon for candidates from the minority fringes of British politics is that they can stand on the podium next to the prime minister when the results are announced on election night.

Conservative constituency chairman John Bridge said the prime minister's constituency always attracted more than its fair share of fringe candidates and the Referendum Party challenge was a waste of time. "The reality is that it will not affect the result one iota," he said.
